title_zh: 我想赢，但你不只是对手
title_en: Wanting to Win, Facing a Person
deck_zh: 你走出了一步我没想到的好棋。我还想赢，却也可能在这一刻看见：那一步是你的，不只是留给我的一道题。
deck_en: You make a move I never saw coming. I still want to win. That need not prevent me from seeing more than a problem to solve.
body_zh: 两个人在公园散步，一个忽然说，跑到那棵树。话音刚落，两个人就跑了出去。跑到一半，前面那个人回头看了一眼，放慢半步。后面的人发现，外侧空出来了：还可以从这里超。
没有报名，没有裁判，他们还是有了一场比赛。起点是刚才站的地方，终点是树，先到的人赢。这几样约好了，却没有约好什么时候提速、谁从哪边超。那些事，要留给跑起来的两个人。
一个人跑，面对的是路、风和自己的腿。另一个人一进来，事情便变了。他也想先到，也在看，也会根据我怎么跑而改变自己。我们要的是同一个位置，而第一名不能同时给两个人。
## 他也在看我怎样看
比赛里多出来的，不只是一具需要超过的身体。我猜他以为我会从内侧走，他也可能正在等我作出这个选择。我预测他的下一步，还得考虑他怎样预测我。对面那个人不是被我算完以后就静止的材料。
不过，猜他会不会加速，与看出眼前还有一条超越的路线，仍是两件事。前者为判断提供材料，后者才是本系列说的判断：规则没有替这一次规定完的可能，被我看见了。至于冲不冲出去、什么时候冲，是接着要作的动作。三样常挨得很近，不必把它们搅成一件事。
这一判也可能错。我以为外侧能超，他下一刻就提速了；或者路比看起来窄。没超过去，不等于刚才没有判断；超过去了，也不能仅凭结果宣布判断有多好。要问的是，这一刻究竟看见了什么，又依据什么。
我想赢，可以只是一时兴起。树到了，笑一阵，接着散步。也可以落在一条更长的线上：我这些年一直在练跑，我希望自己成为跑得快的人，这一场因此与我想成为的样子连在一起。这不是给两种人分高低，只是说，同一句想赢，在不同的人那里，分量可能不一样。
所以，赢了笑、输了哭，还不足以让旁边的人替他把自己说完。一次失利可能碰到了多年努力，也可能只是此刻懊恼；赢后沉默，也不表示他没有在玩。场上的动作、脸上的情绪，给我们材料，却不自动交出一个人的全部理由。
## 那一步，先是他的
换到棋盘边。对手走出一步我没有算到的棋，舍掉一个子，换出一条原来堵住的路。我先前一直在想怎样保子，忽然看见，原来还可以这样走。
看见这条路，是我的判断；那一步棋，却是他的判断。我接下来能不能扳回来，是另一个问题。这几件事能够同时在场，不必因为棋是他下的，便否认我刚才也看见了什么；也不必因为我看懂了，便把他的发现一并拿到自己名下。
我当然还可以想赢。尊重对手，不等于把自己的棋停在那里，或者故意输给他。竞争也没有因此变成合作：这一盘的胜负仍然只能这样分，场上的关系没有被一句好棋改写。
但在争胜之中，我可能不只看到一个待破解的套路，还看见一个自己作判断的人。他不是为了给我的胜利增加难度才存在。他走出了我没看见的一步，这个事实不需要等我下一盘能用它赢回来，才有分量。
这听起来像赛后的握手，或一句真漂亮。可握手也可以只是礼节，赞美也可能是好听的场面话。认输同样只告诉我们，他认下了这次结果，不能直接证明他怎样看待对面的人。
复盘时，区别也不一定马上显出来。一心求胜的人，同样会仔细听对手解释，再据此修改自己的理解。值得继续看的，是对方的想法有没有被当作他的想法听进去，还是只被装进下一盘的情报袋里。我改变的是对这个下棋的人的理解，还是只更新了他的棋路？
这两件事也可能并行。不要因为我仍想赢，就断言我不可能承认他；更不要因为我愿意复盘，就替我颁发尊重别人的证明。后来的谈话能给前一刻提供新材料，却不是一架能够直接照见当时内心的机器。材料不足时，把不足留下，比替人说满更诚实。
赛后两个人一起弄清某一步，复盘本身还可能成了一局合作。活动名称仍叫下棋，彼此所处的关系却换了。分清这种变化，比把整项活动永远贴在竞争或合作的一边更有用。
## 别让一个名称包办整场
职业比赛尤其如此。选手在场上判断怎样出手，也依合同出场，结果连着奖金、收入与资格。游戏与工作可以在同一场里并存。拿钱，不会把每一次场内的发现变成假的；确实在玩，也不会取消他的劳动与合同。
名次和比分本来可以就在规则里面。赢到一座奖杯，与把自己的钱押在这场输赢上，也不是同一种安排。本系列把赌博那一份排除在自己的讨论范围外，按的是局外赌注这条关系，不是说赌钱的人没有判断力。选手自己赌球，排除的是他那一份，不能因此把其余人正常进行的比赛一起抹掉。报名费汇成奖池怎样划，论文仍留着问题；纯由运气决定的局，也没有在这里获得判断力练习的保证。
作弊则把问题推到另一处。两个人以为自己在同一套规则下较量，其中一个却偷偷改了正在发生的事。另一个进入的那一局，与他实际面对的那一局，便不再相同。偷看一张牌，也可能只改了胜算，并没有让每一手从此不必判断。
依本系列的划分，作弊者那一份不再算游戏，仍照原约定在玩的对手，那一份仍是游戏；若所有参与者一起作弊，就没有这样一份留在原来的局中。但这一边界怎样得到充分说明、合谋与大家明着改规则怎样分，论文并没有全部解决。把问题写出来，不等于已经替它完成了证明。
为了赌注而故意输，又不同于看出败局而认输。前者把结果接到了局外的赌注，后者可能只是结束这一盘的动作。只见到输这个结果，不能把两者看成一样；只听见这就是游戏，也不能让偷换约定的那一步消失。
实力悬殊，也不必使一局变空。高手陪新手下，胜负也许早有倾向，新手仍可能第一次看见一条路。可说得清的练习，在他自己看见的这一回，不在旁人替他算出的进步分数里。下次能不能留住，会不会带到局外，都还要另看。
公园里那棵树终于到了。谁先到，是比赛给出的结果；跑到半路发现的那条路，是一个人这一次的判断。对方怎样跑，仍然是对方的事。认真争过，也让这一点留着，我们才不必在只顾赢和假装不想赢之间，替自己选一个过窄的位置。
body_en: Two people are walking in a park. One says, race you to that tree, and they are off. Halfway there, the runner in front glances back and eases slightly. The other sees an opening on the outside: there is another way past.
No registration or referee was necessary. They agreed on a start, a finish, and what would count as winning. They did not agree on every acceleration or route. Those remain with the people running.

Alone, a runner encounters the path, the wind, and their own legs. Competition adds someone who also notices and judges. That person may change course in response to me. We want the same place, and first place cannot belong to both of us.
## Someone who is reading me too

The other runner is not merely a body to overtake. I may think he expects me on the inside; he may be waiting for exactly that choice. Anticipating his next step includes anticipating his anticipation of mine. He does not become still once I have formed an estimate of him.

A forecast remains different from a discovery. Guessing whether he will accelerate supplies material for judgment. Seeing an available route that the agreed rules did not specify is the judgment this series is concerned with. Whether to move, and when, is an action that can follow. They happen close together without being interchangeable.

The judgment can be mistaken. The apparent opening may narrow, or the other runner may accelerate. Failing to pass does not prove there was no judgment; succeeding does not, by itself, certify its quality. We still need to ask what the runner saw and on what basis.

Wanting to win can be a passing intention. Reach the tree, laugh, resume the walk. It can also belong to a longer commitment: I have spent years trying to become a faster runner, and this race touches the person I mean to become. These are different weights the same desire can carry, not ranks assigned to the people carrying them.

A smile after winning or tears after losing cannot settle that difference for us. A loss may touch years of effort, or a momentary frustration. Silence after victory does not establish that the winner was not playing. Actions and emotions give us evidence, not unrestricted access to a person's reasons.
## The move belongs to someone

Now imagine a board between two players. My opponent sacrifices a piece and opens a route I had missed. I was calculating how to preserve that piece. Suddenly I see that giving it up makes something else possible.

Seeing that possibility is my judgment. Finding and making the move was his. Whether I can recover from it is a further question. Understanding his discovery does not transfer its authorship to me; acknowledging its authorship does not erase what I have just discovered.

I can still want to win. Respect need not stop my next move or require a deliberate loss. The match remains competitive: a good word about the other player does not change how its result will be awarded.

Yet I may encounter more than a pattern to defeat. There is a person here, making judgments of his own, not merely existing to make my eventual victory more impressive. His finding a move I missed can matter without waiting to become useful information for beating him next time.

That sounds like a handshake or an admiring remark. Neither proves it. Handshakes can be formalities; compliments can be fluent social performances. Resignation acknowledges the result without revealing everything the resigning player sees in the person opposite.

Analysis afterward does not settle the matter automatically either. A player concerned only with winning can listen closely and revise an understanding of the position. We can ask whether the opponent's explanation is received as his thinking, or only stored as intelligence for the next encounter. Am I revising my understanding of this player as a person, or only my prediction of his moves?

These concerns may coexist. Continuing to seek victory does not establish an inability to recognize the opponent. Agreeing to analyze together does not certify such recognition. A later conversation can illuminate an earlier moment, but is later evidence, not a machine for inspecting the mind as it was then. Where the evidence is insufficient, leaving the question open is more honest than finishing someone else's account.

The analysis can itself become cooperative: two people now want to understand a move together. The activity is still called chess, but their relation has changed. That distinction is more useful than assigning an activity to one permanent box marked competition or cooperation.
## More than one arrangement in a match

Professional sport makes this particularly clear. A player judges a move within the match while also appearing under a contract, with pay, prizes, or eligibility attached to the result. Play and work can coexist. Payment does not make every discovery in the match unreal; genuine playing does not cancel employment and its demands.

Scores and rankings can belong to the rules. Receiving a trophy is not the same arrangement as staking one's own money on the result. This series excludes the gambling share from its chosen scope because of the external stake, not because gamblers make no judgments. A player betting on the match does not erase everyone else's normal participation. Pooled entry fees funding a prize remain an unresolved boundary; activities determined wholly by chance receive no guarantee of exercising judgment here either.

Cheating changes something else. Two people enter what they understand to be the same contest, while one secretly alters what is actually taking place. The game the opponent entered diverges from the game being conducted. Peeking at a card may change the odds without removing every remaining decision or discovery.

Under this series' classification, the cheater's share no longer counts as play, while the opponent continuing under the agreed rules still plays. If all participants cheat, no such share remains in the original game. The paper does not, however, complete the justification for this boundary or settle every distinction between collusion and openly agreeing on new rules. Naming the problem is not the same as having proved the answer.

Deliberately losing for a stake is also different from resigning after recognizing a lost position. One attaches the result to an external bet; the other can be the action that ends this game. The visible result, a loss, cannot identify which occurred. Nor can calling something a game make a concealed alteration of the agreement disappear.

An uneven match need not be empty. A novice playing an expert may have little prospect of victory and still discover a route for the first time. The practice we can identify lies in that actual use of judgment, not in an improvement score assigned from outside. What lasts into another match, or travels beyond play, remains to be examined.

Eventually the runners reach the tree. Who arrived first is the contest's result. The opening noticed halfway there is someone's judgment on this occasion. How the other person runs remains theirs. Taking victory seriously while leaving that fact intact gives us more room than a choice between caring only about winning and pretending not to care at all.
pause_zh: 如果下一局遇见一步意外的好棋，可以留意一下：你新看见了哪条路？对方对那一步的解释，有没有改动你原来的理解？不必用答案给自己或对手打分。
pause_en: If an unexpected move catches you next time, you might notice what possibility it reveals and whether the other person's explanation changes your understanding. The answers need not become a score for either of you.
